for_owner.title: The VOC algorithm: a literal copy of Sensirion's code, or house style?
for_owner.question: Does the VOC algorithm keep upstream's names and order?
for_owner.context: The VOC index algorithm is a line-by-line port of Sensirion's reference code (through DFRobot's translation), checked against upstream test values. The plan exempts it from the repo's naming rules and from your member-ordering rule so it can still be compared side by side with the original. Your ordering decision named only test functions as an exception, and your one-material rule names none, so this exemption needs your word. The firmware behaves the same either way.

options.label: Keep it literal
options.consequence: Upstream names, casing and order stay; it is listed as the one named exception to both rules, and only the class other modules import follows the naming scheme. Easy to diff against Sensirion's code.

options.label: Literal names, house order
options.consequence: Function bodies and names stay as upstream, but functions are sorted like every other module. Still traceable function by function, harder to diff as a whole file.

options.label: Full house style
options.consequence: Renamed and reordered like any module. One material everywhere, but tracing a line back to Sensirion's code needs a name map.
